## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Upāhanāruḷha* ("Wearing sandals") is the sixty-second training rule (*sekhiya*) in the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule regulates monastic decorum regarding teaching, prohibiting a monk from expounding the Dhamma to someone wearing sandals who is not sick [SuttaCentral]. An English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral]. All matches for "SK 62" in the retrieved secondary literature refer to verse 62 of the philosophical treatise *Sāṅkhyakārikā* rather than this Vinaya rule.

Parallels to this training rule are widely attested across early Buddhist monastic traditions [SuttaCentral]. In the Pali tradition, it corresponds directly to *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* *Sekhiya* 62, the *Bhikkhu Parivāra* (*Sekhiya* 62), and the corresponding nuns' Vinaya texts: *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* *Sekhiya* 62, *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* *Sekhiya* 62, and the *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* [SuttaCentral]. Close parallels are also preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan Vinaya collections representing the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsaṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, Kāśyapīya, and Lokottaravāda lineages [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus reflects this formulaic setting, identifying 69 internal Pali reuse passages across 28 texts; its closest structural affinities are with adjacent *Sekhiya* rules concerning appropriate decorum when teaching the Dhamma, particularly *Sekhiya* 72, 65, 66, 67, and 63 [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus registers no cross-language matches exceeding the score threshold [DharmaNexus].
